beats.text: In 2007, scientists sent tiny animals into open space. No suit. No protection.
They were tardigrades, also called water bears, less than a millimeter long.
For ten days they rode on the outside of a satellite, in the vacuum of space.
Back on Earth, many of them woke up. Some even laid eggs that hatched.
Their trick: they dry out, curl into a ball, and almost stop living.
The first animals known to survive open space were smaller than a grain of sand.
